name: I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing

podcast.body: A "massive worldwide hit single" from 1970, which was itself a cover version and directly derived from "one of the most popular and most famous Coca-Cola commercials of all time." Its melody was found to be similar to Oasis's "Shaker Maker," leading to a successful lawsuit against Oasis. "Not only was this a massive worldwide hit single, a cover version was also a big hit around the same time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Originally recorded by the band as a radio jingle with Coca-Cola lyrics for McCann Erickson, it was later released as a single without product references due to popular demand. Their version, sounding more like the original commercial, became the bigger hit between competing releases, peaking at number 7 on the Hot 100 in January 1972 and notably reaching number 1 in the UK. "Since the New Seekers naturally sounded more like the commercial, after all, they'd recorded the original version. There's proved to be the bigger hit."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song, released in 1970, was a "massive worldwide hit single," with a cover version also popular around the same time. It was "derived from one of the most popular and most famous Coca-Cola commercials of all time." The melody was later found to be similar to Oasis's "Shaker Maker," leading to a lawsuit against Oasis. "Not only was this a massive worldwide hit single, a cover version was also a big hit around the same time. And it was all derived from one of the most popular and most famous Coca-Cola commercials of all time."
